description: When a user creates a CV from a job offer, the new CV opens with every field filled. The content is tailored to the offer where the offer allows it. Every other field holds an explicit sample value whose wording shows what belongs there, so the user knows at a glance what to replace. This applies to a saved job application (Mes candidatures) and to Job Search, and the content is written in the offer's language.

userStories.title: A complete CV draft can be built from any job offer
userStories.description: As the product, I want one builder that turns a job offer into a complete resume, so that every CV created from an offer has every field filled the same way.
acceptanceCriteria: Every field. Given a job offer (title, company, location, description) and optional AI content, the builder returns a resume in which every field listed in Context is non-empty, except the photo. This covers title, the 7 contact fields and summary. It covers at least 1 experience with company, position, start and end date, location, description and at least 1 achievement. It covers 1 education with school, degree, field, dates, GPA, description and at least 1 achievement. It covers at least 1 skill category with content, at least 1 language with a level, and 1 certification with name, issuer, date, expiry date, credential id and URL. It covers at least 1 project with name, description, URL, dates and at least 1 technology. Every entry is visible.
Offer data first. The title (headline) is the job title. The contact location is the job's location when it has one. The summary names the job title, or the job title and company.
AI content where available. When AI content is given, its summary, experiences, skills and projects are used, and any of their fields left empty is filled from the sample set.

Sample values describe their field. Each sample value makes the field's purpose obvious without the label. Examples for fr: name "Prénom Nom", email "prenom.nom@exemple.com", phone "+41 00 000 00 00", LinkedIn "linkedin.com/in/votre-profil"; school "Nom de votre école", certification "Nom de votre certification". Equivalent sets exist in en, de and it. No sample value names a real person, company or institution.
One language per CV. The builder takes a content language (fr, en, de or it), and every sample value in the result comes from that one set.
Valid formats. Dates are `YYYY-MM`, email and URLs are well-formed, language levels are stored values, and rich-text fields are sanitized HTML that renders in all five templates.

FR-1: One builder, used by both entry points. Sample values are defined once per language. No second copy of the resume shape or of the sample values is introduced (`.claude/rules/resumes.md`, `CLAUDE.md` §10).

FR-2: The sample values are product content requested by the owner, not test fixtures. They live in their own module with a comment stating that intent. They must not reuse `e2e/fixtures/resume.ts`, and they must differ from `TEMPLATE_SAMPLE_RESUME` in style: values that describe their field, not a realistic invented person.
FR-3: The application is read server-side with the user's session, and ownership is enforced. The client never sends job content that the server trusts for the application path.
FR-4: AI output and offer text are untrusted. Rich text is sanitized before storage or rendering with the project's existing path; lengths stay within the existing input limits.

FR-5: The AI test stub is enabled only by an explicit server env flag set in the Playwright web server config. It is ignored when `NODE_ENV` is `production` or the request is not local, and it has a unit test proving it cannot activate in production.
FR-6: No schema migration and no new dependency.
FR-7: New UI strings exist, non-empty, in fr, en, de and it (`src/locales/locale-parity.test.ts`).
Regression constraint: Creating a CV without a job (`/dashboard/resumes/new` with no `jobApplicationId`) stays exactly as today: empty content, template picker, title required.

Regression constraint: The template picker (`e2e/template-picker*.spec.ts`), the adaptation modal (`e2e/adaptation-modal-*.spec.ts`), Job Search mobile and the job-applications specs pass unchanged, apart from added content assertions.
Regression constraint: Existing CVs are not modified.
Regression constraint: Exports (PDF, Word) and parity are unchanged. `pnpm test:parity` stays NEW 0 / KNOWN 3, and the Word generators get no diff.
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline, plus `pnpm test:parity`.

Verification: Unit tests: the builder returns every field non-empty (except the photo) for an offer with AI content and for one without; each of the four sample sets is complete and in one language; formats are valid; AI content takes precedence and its gaps are filled; the language falls back for an unsupported or undetectable language; the stub cannot activate in production.

Verification: e2e with the server-side AI stub, in fr and de: Mes candidatures creates a complete, linked CV, with the language taken from a German offer opened under `/fr`; an application with no description, and the AI failing, still produce a complete CV and show the notice; another user's application is refused; Job Search creates a complete CV; the editor shows every section filled, read from the stored row and the rendered editor.
Verification: `export-validation`: the PDF and Word of a CV created from an offer contain every section, checked on the generated artifacts.
Verification: `security-review` on the new server path, ownership, sanitization and the stub guard.
Verification: `ui-expert` on the creation page and the new CV in the editor and Preview, in fr and de at 1440 and 375, all five templates for one created CV. `code-reviewer`.

acceptanceCriteria: Title. Opening `/[locale]/dashboard/resumes/new?jobApplicationId=<id>` pre-fills the CV title from the application's job title. The user can still change it, and still choose a template.

Complete content. Submitting creates a CV filled through the US-001 builder. When the application has a usable description, AI content in the offer's language is used. The CV opens in the editor with every section showing its content.
Language. The content language is the offer's language when it is fr, en, de or it, otherwise the UI locale. A German offer opened from `/fr/...` gives a German CV.

No description, or AI failure. If the application has no usable description, or the AI fails or is rate-limited, the CV is still created, complete with sample values and the job's own fields. The user sees a short notice in the page language that the content could not be tailored.
Link and ownership. The CV is linked to the application, both ways, as today. A request for another user's application, or a missing one, is refused server-side and creates nothing.
Banner and validation. The banner ("CV pour la candidature … chez …") and the title-required message read in fr, de and it, and en is unchanged.
Feedback. While the CV is generated, the submit button shows a localized busy state and cannot be submitted twice.
